title: Geo-fanout weight inversion causing hosted->dedicated routing regressions
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several customers experienced sudden routing regressions where requests that should have stayed on hosted model variants were routed to Dedicated pools or incompatible private variants, resulting in elevated latency, token rejections, and a few data-mismatch errors for strict schema outputs. This ticket tracks the investigation, short-term mitigations, and the permanent fix for the geo-fanout weight aggregation bug that inverted regional weights during policy merges.

Scope & impact: Affected tenants spanned Hosted and Dedicated customers (mix of low-latency and enterprise workloads). Symptoms included: 1) unexpected model variant (quantized vs full-precision) selection; 2) cross-region failovers even when local capacity existed; 3) 5-15% error/timeout spike and 2x median latency for impacted routes. Customer Success logged three high-severity escalations during the window.

Root cause hypothesis (finalized): A recent change to fallback policy merging introduced a new aggregation step for geo-fanout weights. When a policy had zero-weight regions combined with tenant-level overrides, the normalization code applied an integer floor before normalization, and the intermediate negative delta from a tenant override caused the highest-weighted region to be reduced to zero and other regions to be normalized upward (weight inversion). In short: incorrect handling of negative deltas + integer truncation produced an inversion in the final routing weights.

Why this escaped tests: Unit tests validated pairwise merges but not multi-policy geo-fanout merges with mixed zero/negative deltas and tenant overrides. Integration tests did not cover real-world policy sets used by enterprise customers.

Fix summary: 1) Correct the aggregation routine to keep floating-point deltas until normalization and enforce stable sort on region priority to break ties. 2) Add defensive checks to prevent any weight < 0 after merge. 3) Add migration to re-evaluate currently stored merged policies and re-publish corrected weight vectors to router cache. 4) Add unit and integration tests that mirror enterprise policy shapes. 5) Canary deploy with additional telemetry.

Rollback/mitigation: Emergency mitigation applied at 2026-03-07T04:12Z: an emergency tenant-pin rule was pushed for affected tenants to prefer hosted endpoints explicitly (bypassing aggregated weights). That reduced customer impact while a patch was prepared.

Acceptance criteria: 1) Misroute rate for affected tenants drops to baseline (<0.1% of requests) in canary and full rollout. 2) No new negative-weight policy entries in policy store. 3) Canaryed for 24 hours on 10%/50%/100% progression with no regression signals. 4) New tests added and green in CI.

Longer-term follow-ups: Policy simulation harness to exercise combinations of tenant overrides + region weights, documentation for policy authors about non-zero floors, add telemetry that surfaces weight inversions as an anomaly.

postmortem_notes: Preliminary: policy merge code change went through QA but lacked realistic policy fixtures. Root cause: fragile integer rounding + negative-delta semantics. Corrective actions: 1) add policy simulation harness; 2) add CI gate that runs sample enterprise policy set daily; 3) improve alerting semantics to catch inversion anomalies earlier.
